# core/hashmap.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/hashmap.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

A hash map from `u64` keys to values of any type
`V` that can be copied (`u64`, `Span`, a struct of numbers, ...).

Open addressing with linear probing and tombstones. Every function takes
the value type as its type argument: `hmap_new[u64]()`,
`hmap_insert[Span](&mut m, k, s)`. To map keys to linear values
(buffers, structs owning pages), keep the values in a `Vec[T]` and map
each key to its index: a `HashMap[V]` with a linear `V` is rejected
where a function copies a value.

What is proved: every index is in bounds, no counter overflows, `len`
is the number of keys and `used` the number of slots that are not
empty, a slot that a lookup returns holds the key asked for, and after
`hmap_insert` the map holds the key with the new value. Not proved: that
a lookup finds every key present (that needs an invariant about runs of
probed slots).

`import "core/hashmap.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md).

| [`hmap_with_cap`](#hmap_with_cap) | An empty map with room for `cap` slots (at least 8). |
| [`hmap_new`](#hmap_new) | An empty map with room for 8 keys before it grows. |
| [`hmap_len`](#hmap_len) | The number of keys in the map (`hmap_ok` says `len` counts them). |
| [`hmap_contains`](#hmap_contains) | `k` is in the map. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `HashMap`

```bastio
struct HashMap[V] {
  keys: Vec[u64],
  vals: Vec[Option[V]],   // None in a slot that has never held a key
  tags: Vec[u8],   // 0 empty, 1 removed (a tombstone), 2 holds a key
  len: u64,        // slots holding a key
  used: u64,       // slots holding a key or a tombstone
}
```

## Functions

### `hash_u64`

```bastio
fn hash_u64(k: u64) -> u64
```

A 64-bit mixing function (the finalizer of MurmurHash3), so that keys
that differ only in high bits still spread over the table.

### `hmap_with_cap`

```bastio
fn hmap_with_cap[V](cap: u64) -> HashMap[V]
  requires 8 <= cap && cap <= 1152921504606846976
  ensures hmap_ok[V](result) && result.len == 0 && vlen(result.keys) == cap
```

An empty map with room for `cap` slots (at least 8).

Example:

```bastio
// A loop that changes a map says it stays well formed.
let mut m = hmap_with_cap[u64](1024);
let mut i = 0;
while i < 1000
  invariant i <= 1000 && hmap_ok[u64](m)
{
  let prev = hmap_insert[u64](&mut m, hash_u64(i), i);
  i = i + 1;
}
let gone = hmap_remove[u64](&mut m, hash_u64(5));
let keys = hmap_keys[u64](m);   // every key in the map, in slot order
let ok = gone is Option::Some && vec_len(keys) == 999 && hmap_len[u64](m) == 999;
vec_free(keys);
hmap_free[u64](m);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `hmap_new`

```bastio
fn hmap_new[V]() -> HashMap[V]
  ensures hmap_ok[V](result) && result.len == 0
```

An empty map with room for 8 keys before it grows.

Example:

```bastio
// Process id to parent id.
let mut m = hmap_new[u64]();
let a = hmap_insert[u64](&mut m, 100, 1);
let b = hmap_insert[u64](&mut m, 101, 100);
let c = hmap_insert[u64](&mut m, 101, 1);   // replaces, and returns the old value
assert hmap_maps[u64](m, 101, 1);            // proved: the map holds the new value
let mut ok = a is Option::None && b is Option::None && opt_or[u64](c, 0) == 100;
// A lookup that finds a key is proved to return its value; that it finds
// every key is not proved, so the `None` arm stays.
match hmap_get[u64](m, 100) {
  Option::Some(v) => { ok = ok && v == 1; },
  Option::None => { ok = false; },
}
ok = ok && hmap_len[u64](m) == 2 && hmap_contains[u64](m, 101) && hmap_get_or[u64](m, 7, 0) == 0;
hmap_free[u64](m);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `hmap_len`

```bastio
fn hmap_len[V](m: &HashMap[V]) -> u64
  ensures result == m.len
```

The number of keys in the map (`hmap_ok` says `len` counts them).

### `hmap_contains`

```bastio
fn hmap_contains[V](m: &HashMap[V], k: u64) -> bool
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures result ==> hmap_has[V](m, k)
```

`k` is in the map.

### `hmap_get`

```bastio
fn hmap_get[V](m: &HashMap[V], k: u64) -> Option[V]
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> hmap_maps[V](m, k, result.Some)
```

The value of `k`.

### `hmap_get_or`

```bastio
fn hmap_get_or[V](m: &HashMap[V], k: u64, d: V) -> V
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures result == d || hmap_maps[V](m, k, result)
```

The value of `k`, or `d` if `k` is not in the map.

### `hmap_insert`

```bastio
fn hmap_insert[V](m: &mut HashMap[V], k: u64, v: V) -> Option[V]
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures hmap_ok[V](m) && hmap_maps[V](m, k, v)
```

Sets the value of `k` to `v`. Returns the value it replaces, if `k` was
already in the map.

### `hmap_remove`

```bastio
fn hmap_remove[V](m: &mut HashMap[V], k: u64) -> Option[V]
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures hmap_ok[V](m)
```

Takes `k` out of the map. Returns its value, if it was there.

### `hmap_keys`

```bastio
fn hmap_keys[V](m: &HashMap[V]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures forall j: u64 :: j < vlen(result) ==> hmap_has[V](m, vget(result, j))
```

The keys in the map, in slot order.

### `hmap_free`

```bastio
fn hmap_free[V](m: HashMap[V])
```

Frees the map. Values that own nothing are simply dropped.

## Specification functions

### `hmap_ok`

```bastio
spec fn hmap_ok[V](m: &HashMap[V]) -> bool {
  vlen(m.tags) == vlen(m.keys) && vlen(m.vals) == vlen(m.keys)
    && 8 <= vlen(m.keys) && vlen(m.keys) <= 1152921504606846976
    && vcount(m.tags, 0) + vcount(m.tags, 1) + vcount(m.tags, 2) == vlen(m.tags)
    && m.len == vcount(m.tags, 2) && m.used + vcount(m.tags, 0) == vlen(m.tags)
    && m.len <= m.used && m.used < vlen(m.keys)
}
```

What every map function needs and keeps: the vectors have one length,
the capacity is in range, every tag is 0, 1 or 2, `len` counts the
slots holding a key and `used` the slots that are not empty, and some
slot is still empty. A loop that changes a map carries
`invariant hmap_ok[V](m)`.

### `hmap_maps`

```bastio
spec fn hmap_maps[V](m: &HashMap[V], k: u64, v: V) -> bool {
  !(forall i: u64 :: i < vlen(m.keys) ==>
      !(vget(m.tags, i) == 2 && vget(m.keys, i) == k
        && vget(m.vals, i) is Option::Some && vget(m.vals, i).Some == v))
}
```

The map holds key `k` with value `v`.

### `hmap_has`

```bastio
spec fn hmap_has[V](m: &HashMap[V], k: u64) -> bool {
  !(forall i: u64 :: i < vlen(m.keys) ==> !(vget(m.tags, i) == 2 && vget(m.keys, i) == k))
}
```

The map holds key `k`.

## Internals

### `hmap_find`

```bastio
fn hmap_find[V](m: &HashMap[V], k: u64) -> u64
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures result <= vlen(m.keys)
  ensures result < vlen(m.keys) ==> vget(m.tags, result) == 2 && vget(m.keys, result) == k
```

Internal: The slot holding `k`, or the capacity if `k` is not in the map.

### `hmap_grow`

```bastio
fn hmap_grow[V](m: &mut HashMap[V])
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures hmap_ok[V](m)
```

Internal: Rebuilds the table without tombstones, doubling it when at least half
of it holds keys.

### `hmap_put_new`

```bastio
fn hmap_put_new[V](m: &mut HashMap[V], k: u64, v: V)
  requires hmap_ok[V](m)
  ensures hmap_ok[V](m) && hmap_maps[V](m, k, v)
```

Internal: Puts `k`, known not to be in the map, into the first empty slot of its
probe sequence, growing the table first if it is three quarters used.
